thread:
emma (Design): Usability quick note: charts with smoothing are masking short actionable spikes. testers missed 10-20s blips. We should expose a lightweight option instead of switching global default.

zack (PM): Agree. Prefer a per-panel option. What about a "compact peak annotations" mode that marks preserved spikes with a small unobtrusive glyph and summary badge in legend?

mira (Viz Eng): Built a prototype: `compact_peak_annotations` uses prominence + MAD to decide preserves, then renders small hollow diamonds capped at 5 per-series. Config snippet:
```
annotations:
  mode: compact_peak_annotations
  cap: 5
  prominence_factor: 2.5
```
Keeps the timeline clean but surfaces short spikes.

ivan (A11y): Accessibility: glyphs must be keyboard-focusable and have an `aria-label` like "peak +230ms at 14:12 UTC". Also don't rely on color: add a shape + dash pattern for high contrast / colorblind palettes. Current orange diamond fails contrast on dark theme.

emma (Design): Copy: toggle label = "Show short spikes". Legend microcopy: show a tiny "spikes" badge when preserved spikes exist; hide badge otherwise. Keep full config behind a chevron to avoid clutter.

zack (PM): Thresholds need metric-awareness (percent vs absolute). Default to `auto` but allow manual override per-panel. We should also surface telemetry: preserved spikes count per-panel to tune defaults.

mira (Viz Eng): Impl notes: two-line condensed legend (name + microstate) keeps layout tight. Performance: cap markers and prefer canvas rendering for markers to avoid DOM bloat. Add debug overlay for QA showing preserved indices.

ivan (A11y): Add keyboard shortcut: press "K" to cycle annotation states for focused chart. Tooltip "K: toggle spike annotations" and strong focus ring. Ensure screen readers announce state changes.

ui-bot: Mock uploaded: https://redwood.design/mockups/compact_peak_annotations_v1.png

emma (Design): I'll update component spec and open PR with QA checklist: keyboard nav, screen reader labels, color contrast checks, legend truncation, metric-adaptive thresholds, and performance cap tests.
